🇲🇽✈️ <u>MEXICO BREAKS FIVE TOURISM RECORDS IN FIRST HALF OF 2026</u>

51.1 million international travelers came to Mexico from January to June — 7.7% more than last year — including 24.5 million tourists, $18.8 billion in revenue and 6.6 million cruise passengers. All historic highs. While the usual voices sell Mexico as a "failed state," the world keeps booking flights. Sheinbaum's goal is the top 5 of global destinations: "Come to Mexico, a marvelous country — it's in fashion."

🇲🇽🥑 <u>US FULLY REOPENS MICHOACÁN AVOCADO EXPORTS — DIALOGUE BEATS ULTIMATUMS</u>

Washington suspended avocado inspections in Michoacán over "security concerns." Mexico didn't escalate or cave — it negotiated. Agriculture Secretary Columba López announced the full resumption: "Thanks to the dialogue tables and joint work between authorities of Mexico and the United States, today, August 13, inspection and export of avocados in Michoacán fully resumes." Mexico's most iconic export moves again.

🇲🇽✊ 505 years after the defense of Tenochtitlan: Mexican women still defend sovereignty. "A day like today, August 13, 505 years ago, Mexica women and men defended their city, their territory, their ways of life. Today, 505 years later, Mexican women continue defending the sovereignty of this country." — Noemí Juárez, Undersecretary of Basic Education On August 13, 1521, Tenochtitlan fell after an 80-day siege. The mañanera's "Women in History" segment honored the women of that defense and the indigenous women who preserved language and ancestral knowledge.

🚨🇲🇽 ICE plans electric-shock gauntlets for raids. Mexico has filed complaints over deaths in US detention. "We do not agree with raids or with the violation of the human rights of any person — particularly of a Mexican who went to the United States to earn a living." — President Claudia Sheinbaum Foreign Secretary Roberto Velasco will detail next Wednesday the complaints filed over the deaths of Mexicans in ICE custody and during detentions.
banner: ICE SHOCK GAUNTLET: MEXICO FILES COMPLAINTS

text: 🔥🇲🇽 PRI leader asks Washington to strip visas from Mexico's electoral officials. "The president of a near-extinct political party goes to the United States to ask them to take away visas. He no longer believes in Mexico, nor in Mexicans." — President Claudia Sheinbaum Alejandro Moreno filed a complaint with the US State Department after electoral authorities sanctioned him. Meanwhile, the Campeche state prosecutor is detaining former officials from his time as governor.

🇲🇽📺 79% of Mexicans back sanctioning media that deceive audiences, national poll shows. "As President López Obrador used to say: 'Fool is he who thinks the people are fools.'" — President Claudia Sheinbaum Poll presented at the mañanera: 78% say outlets must clearly separate news, opinion and paid content; 86% back regulating minors' access to social networks. The government's actual proposal: a code of ethics and an audience ombudsman in each outlet.
banner: "FOOL IS HE WHO THINKS THE PEOPLE ARE FOOLS"

text: 🔥🇲🇽 PAN demands a "right of reply" slot inside the mañanera. Sheinbaum: build your own space. "Everyone has their own space. This is the people's space — the people's mañanera. If people watch us, it's because they like it." — President Claudia Sheinbaum The PAN's congressional group formally requested airtime in the daily press conference to counter "false facts." Sheinbaum recalled the PRIAN candidate's own morning show in 2024 — it didn't last.

🇲🇽📈 Customs revenue hits 2026 record: 131 billion pesos collected in July. "Customs that only worked 10 hours a day now work 24. Around a thousand young people were hired — new, without any vices. That has helped a lot." — President Claudia Sheinbaum The National Customs Agency reported its highest monthly collection of the year. New 24/7 operations, faster cargo clearance, and a monitoring center in Querétaro.
